description: The Prez (WagerTalk) review, checked 20 Nov 2026: prices from $25 to $1,999, a credit only guarantee, streak claims checked and what bettors say.
dek: A WagerTalk handicapper who goes only by "The Prez", sold picks on Who2BetOn.com as far back as 2005, and is described by WagerTalk as one of its co-founders. Packages run from $25 a play to $1,999 for a year. The guarantee pays in site credit, and the records on show are streaks chosen and graded by the seller.

short_answer: The Prez is a real, long running handicapper brand. Saved copies of Who2beton.com show him selling picks there in 2005, 2010 and 2013, with an "Ask The Prez" page, and his WagerTalk bio calls him "The Founder and CEO of Who2beton." Since about 2020 that site has said it is "rebuilding" and sends visitors to WagerTalk, where on 20 Nov 2026 his profile posted daily picks, priced every package and showed a table of his last 20 graded plays.

Whether the picks make money over time is a separate question, and nothing we could open answers it. The sales copy leads with runs such as "77-38 (67%)" on totals and "72-39" in the NHL, each starting where the seller chose. The Last 20 table on the same profile showed 9 wins and 11 losses on 20 Nov 2026, the same as on 16 Nov, and his five NHL plays in it went one and four.

WagerTalk's own copy calls The Prez one of its co-founders, and its press releases name Lawrence Prezman as co-founder and, in 2019, its President. The profile never says the two are the same person, but either way the company that grades and promotes his record is not a neutral party. We found almost no independent buyer posts about him. Treat the numbers as marketing until you have tracked his picks yourself.

guarantee: WagerTalk sells most daily plays in two versions: a plain price and a higher "Guaranteed" price ($25.00 versus $38.00 on 20 Nov 2026). The terms box says the option "backs your purchase with 100% in credits. If your daily pick(s) package does not result in an overall profit across all included plays, the paid cash value of a guaranteed pick will be credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase." It is not cash back, and it costs about 50% more.

The WagerTalk refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold "as is"", with no refund once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed. The terms say the company's entire liability is "a refund of the price paid or replacement of our products, at our option." We saw no guarantee attached to the multi day or season passes. Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves, which are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: Every streak starts where the seller chose to start it, and "units" depend on how big each bet is rated. When we did the arithmetic the printed percentages were right, but the same totals run appears as 77-38 in one box and 77-37 in another, and as 64% and 65% since 1 Dec 2025.

The Hot Streaks box was last updated on 12 Nov 2026. In the week that followed, the Last 20 table on the same profile showed his NHL plays at 1 and 4, while the box still led with NHL runs. A streak box that is not updated after losses only ever shows the good part.

No real name appears on the profile. A WagerTalk bio for another handicapper calls The Prez "one of our co-founders at Wagertalk." WagerTalk press releases name Lawrence Prezman as a co-founder (2018), as "WagerTalk President" (2019) and as continuing in a business development role when WagerTalk Media was formed (2020). The nickname fits, but we have no statement tying the two together, so we treat it as a likely link, not a fact.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. The Prez does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming The Prez most often were WagerTalkPicks, SteveMerril, teddy_covers, BuzzKill (TheRX newsletters thread). From 20 Sep 2026 to 17 Nov 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a The Prez block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.

Result: 13 plays, 7 won, 6 lost, +0.13 units, a return of +1.0% per unit risked. By sport: NHL 1 won, 4 lost, -3.09 units; NFL 3 won, 1 lost, +1.73 units; NCAAF 3 won, 1 lost, +1.49 units. By month: September 5 won, 0 lost, +4.31 units; October 2 won, 2 lost, -0.18 units; November 0 won, 4 lost, -4.00 units.

What it means: a 54% win rate on 13 decided plays has a 95% range of about 29% to 77%, and at the prices in this sample a bettor needed about 53% to break even. That range includes break even, so this sample cannot show whether they win or lose over time. The sample covers only the plays that others chose to post, which is not the full card a subscriber receives, and stakes are counted flat even where the seller rates plays differently.
Another 1 plays naming The Prez first appeared after the game had started, so they are not counted; they went 0 won, 1 lost, -1.00 units.

What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick by The Prez kept by a third party, no contest results, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: a Last 20 table, a Hot Streaks box and a Who's Hot leaderboard. On 20 Nov 2026 the Last 20 table covered plays from 14 to 19 Nov and showed 9 wins and 11 losses. Leaving out the parlay, whose price is not shown, we priced the other 19 plays at the odds listed: 8 wins and 11 losses, about 4 units behind if each risked one unit. The Who's Hot boxes put him first in college basketball for the last 30 days (10-3, +$2,046) and third in the NFL (16-6, +$2,051). All of these are graded by WagerTalk, the company that sells the picks and that its own copy says he helped found.

He also posts free picks with written analysis on the profile, and WagerTalk's social accounts announce them several times a week. Free picks are a fair way to judge his reasoning, but a handful of them is not a record.

Background: who2beton.com was registered on 9 Mar 2000. A saved copy from 1 Jan 2005 lists The Prez first among about twenty handicappers, with an "Ask The Prez" page, a 24 hour support line and a record line for him of 65-50 (56.5%) +31.2. A January 2010 copy advertised his college basketball card for $29, and a 2013 copy still lists him among the experts. By January 2020 the site read "We're currently rebuilding Who2BetOn, big things are on the way but for now, please visit www.wagertalk.com", and a July 2026 copy says the same. WagerTalk was founded in July 2015, bought Sportsmemo in 2018 and The Gold Sheet newsletter in 2019, formed WagerTalk Media in 2020 under chief executive Rick Allec, and partnered with Picks and Parlays and WinnersAndWhiners in 2025. The Prez profile is also listed on the Picks and Parlays store.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence about The Prez is close to nonexistent. Most public posts that mention him are WagerTalk's own free pick announcements. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found one independent post that speaks to The Prez himself: a 2026 post on X from someone who said they had known him since his Who2BetOn days and had invested in that venture, made no money, but found him honest. Everything else is about WagerTalk as a whole. Two Reddit posts from November 2024, a TheRX thread from September 2026 and more than a dozen CapperTek reviews from 2021 to 2026 describe buyers losing with other WagerTalk handicappers, and TheRX has barred all WagerTalk cappers, and The Prez by name, from its free service play threads since at least March 2023. A 2025 Gambling911 article reported a public dispute in which a bettor promised to "expose" WagerTalk, with no verified findings. None of the buyer posts names The Prez, so they say nothing about his picks in particular, though the same complaint about WagerTalk handicappers recurs across sites and years. We found no positive buyer report about his paid packages either. Our Reddit coverage is partial: the Reddit archive's full text search timed out on 20 Nov 2026, so we relied on our saved copy of several betting subreddits and direct archive reads of the threads below.

A user on X wrote that they had known The Prez since he ran Who2BetOn before WagerTalk, that they invested in it and did not make any money, but that he was honest. No details or figures were given, and we could not verify the account. We read this from our saved library copy and do not link posts on X.

On Reddit, a buyer posted a warning about WagerTalk in general, saying they had tried several different handicappers there over about a year and a half, contacted support, and none of them topped 50%. Another reply said streaks are normal for any handicapper. The post does not name The Prez.

A Reddit user said they paid about $1,200 to $1,300 for a year pass with one WagerTalk handicapper and believed they were down, and had stopped betting a second WagerTalk handicapper's package. Neither was The Prez.

CapperTek lists more than a dozen reviews of WagerTalk.com dated from March 2021 to October 2026. The ones we read describe advertised records that did not hold up after purchase. None of the visible reviews mentions The Prez.

A TheRX member asked for a WagerTalk handicapper recommendation, saying they had followed one of the network's soccer handicappers for a couple of years without making a profit. Nobody had replied when we read it. It does not concern The Prez, though that handicapper's WagerTalk bio says The Prez talked him into joining.

TheRX service play guidelines tell members not to post picks from "All Wagertalk Cappers" and list The Prez by name among both the barred services and the barred write ups. The rule is repeated at the top of each daily thread. In October 2026 a moderator added that Gold Sheet plays were barred on word from "the higher ups", and a member guessed it was because the Gold Sheet is part of WagerTalk. No reason is given in the rules.

Gambling911 reported that a sports bettor had promised on X to "expose" WagerTalk and one of its co-owners on a live audio show, that WagerTalk blocked them, and that the bettor posted a message they said came from someone close to that co-owner calling their posts false and defamatory. Gambling911 said it "cannot independently verify any claims" and that it has close relations with some people at WagerTalk. The article does not mention The Prez, and we found no follow up showing what, if anything, was proven.

Searches of the Reddit archive, TheRX, Covers, Sportsbook Review and the web found no thread reviewing The Prez by name, and no buyer posting a long record of his paid picks. Who2beton.com still shows only a "rebuilding" notice.

conflicts: WagerTalk grades The Prez's picks, ranks him on its own leaderboards and sells his packages. A WagerTalk bio for another handicapper calls him one of the company's co-founders. The records on his profile therefore come from the seller's side of the deal.
TheRX's free pick threads bar all WagerTalk handicappers and The Prez by name, so the usual way buyers compare paid plays in public is closed for him.

The free picks he posts double as advertising for paid packages, and the WagerTalk site also runs sportsbook promo code pages. That proves nothing about his picks, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.
strengths: Sold through a company with a Las Vegas mailing address, written terms and a public corporate history in press releases.
A long public trail: listed on Who2beton.com by January 2005, so he is not a new name.
Every package has a published price, and daily plays come with an optional credit guarantee.
He posts free picks with full written reasoning, and the profile shows a Last 20 table that includes losses.
We found no complaints, court cases or regulator actions that name him.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a streak, a short window or a total chosen by the seller.
WagerTalk describes him as one of its co-founders, so the grading and the rankings are not independent.
The streak box was not updated after a 1 and 4 week in the NHL, and the same totals run is printed two different ways on one page.
The guarantee pays in site credit, only on daily packages, never in cash, and costs about 50% more.
The bio says two decades on one page and one decade on another, the profile gives no real name, and we found almost no independent buyer reports about his paid picks.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Check the date on any streak box against the Last 20 table; recent losses may not be in the streak yet.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. On WagerTalk the guarantee is a credit for a future purchase.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, long running WagerTalk handicapper with published prices, daily picks and a company address behind the sales, and saved copies show him selling picks on Who2beton.com since at least 2005. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only records on show are graded by WagerTalk itself, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
What does the Watchdog sample of The Prez show?

We graded 13 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 20 Sep 2026 to 17 Nov 2026: 7 won, 6 lost, +0.13 units at one unit each. The 95% range of the win rate is about 29% to 77%, against about 53% needed to break even.
How much does The Prez cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 single plays cost $25.00, or $38.00 with the credit guarantee. Passes ran $39.00 for a day, $99.00 for a week, $299.00 for 30 days and $1,999.00 for a year, with a one payment year promotion at $1188.00 and season passes from $259.00 to $719.00.
Does The Prez have a verified record?

No. His profile shows streaks such as 77-38 on totals and 72-39 in the NHL, leaderboard ranks, and a Last 20 table that stood at 9 wins and 11 losses on 20 Nov 2026, all graded by WagerTalk. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

The profile gives no real name. His bio says he founded and ran Who2beton.com, and another WagerTalk bio calls him one of WagerTalk's co-founders. WagerTalk press releases name Lawrence Prezman as a co-founder and former President, but the profile does not say they are the same person.
Why can't I find The Prez picks on TheRX?
TheRX's service play rules bar all WagerTalk handicappers and list The Prez by name, so members are told not to repost his plays. The rules give no reason.

For the money you get every play he releases in the period you buy, with written analysis, and on guaranteed daily plays a credit if the day loses. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
